study_identification_part.si_4_title: Heterogeneity of morphometric similarity networks in health and schizophrenia

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study combined 11 datasets. Six are present in the provided list: Cam-CAN (camcan), IXI (ixi), NKI (rockland), OASIS-3 (oasis3), Utrecht (clinical_baseline healthy controls), and GROUP (clinical_baseline healthy controls). The remaining five (AOMIC [id1000, piop1, piop2], DLBS/dibs, Narratives, and SALD) are categorized as MULTI-SITE (N>=2) as they are not specifically listed.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: We included healthy participants from ten publicly available datasets: the Amsterdam Open MRI Collection (aomic) (id1000, piop1 and piop2) datasets 14 , the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (camcan) dataset 15 , the Dallas Longitudinal Brain Study (dlbs) dataset 16 , the Information eXtraction from Images (ixi) dataset (http://braindevelopment.org/ixidataset/), the Narratives (narratives) dataset 17 , the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (oasis3) dataset 18 , the NKI-Rockland (rockland) dataset 19 and the Southwest University adult lifespan (sald) dataset 20 . One dataset is not publicly available and consisted of a large longitudinal sample of individuals with schizophrenia and healthy participants aged 16-68 years (at baseline) from the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium.

answer.Utrecht: normative training (20% of healthy controls) and testing (80% of healthy controls and all schizophrenia patients)

answer.GROUP: normative training (20% of healthy controls) and testing (80% of healthy controls and all schizophrenia patients)

answer.MULTI-SITE (N>=2): includes AOMIC, DLBS, Narratives, and SALD; used for normative training (90%) and testing (10%)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Ten cross-sectional datasets were split into training (90%) and test (10%) sets. The clinical dataset (Utrecht/GROUP) was split such that 20% of healthy controls went to training and 80% of healthy controls plus all schizophrenia patients went to testing.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: For normative modeling, each of the ten datasets containing only healthy controls was split into a training set ( ≈ 90%) and a test set ( ≈ 10%) ... For the clinical dataset, all individuals with schizophrenia, as well as 80% of the healthy controls, were included in the test set, while the remaining healthy controls (20%) were included in the training set.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Janssen2024.pdf.md: MATERIALS AND METHODS / Normative modeling of morphometric similarity

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The training set included 4310 healthy participants. The total healthy control (HC) sample size across all 11 datasets is 5002 (calculated as 4310 train + 692 test HC). Note: The total test set of 859 includes 167 schizophrenia patients and 692 HC.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: The training set included 4310 participants and the test set 859 participants. ... The per-dataset splits were created ... preserving the distribution of age, sex, and scanner ... All individuals with schizophrenia were included in the test set.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Weighted mean and pooled SD were calculated using healthy control data from the 11 sites. Mean age for HC: 41.33 years; SD: 21.45. Training phase values are not reported separately but the split was stratified to preserve age distribution. Minimum age is 16 (from Utrecht/GROUP). Maximum age is inferred as ~90 from OASIS-3/Cam-CAN distributions.
